report_md:
# Report: CPI/NFP release windows on TQQQ

**Strategy:** `family-cpi-nfp-release`
**Window:** development only, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 1-minute marks, next-open
fills, 2% band, idle BIL.
**Bar:** TQQQ dev 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (brief). The panel's
1 bp TQQQ buy-and-hold is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80.

## Verdict

**Negative as a standalone strategy; positive as an event study and a
diversifier.** The centre holds TQQQ only on the CPI proxy session and earns
**10.14% CAGR / 26.16% max DD / 0.65 Sharpe at 1 bp**, falling to **5.46% /
32.27% / 0.40 at 10 bp**. It cannot replace TQQQ and is 26.5 pp below the CAGR
bar. But the CPI-day conditional mean is **+81.9 bp (t = 1.94, n = 96)** and is
positive in all eight years; the correlation to the nine current winners is only
**0.094-0.234**. The NFP day, by contrast, is flat (+6.7 bp, t = 0.15). The
family is a clean example of a real but small event window that is too
low-exposure to be a return engine.

The important honesty check: the CPI-day edge is **not intraday**. The CPI
session's open-to-close return is only +3.9 bp (t = 0.13); the +81.9 bp
open-to-open comes almost entirely from the **close-to-next-open** gap
(~+78 bp). Because the proxy is fixed at calendar day 12 and the actual CPI
release is usually a few days later, the overnight may be capturing the actual
release morning. The strategy is still ex-ante and tradable, but the
"release-day drift" label is too strong; it is a mid-month overnight window.
NFP, which has an actual fixed release date (first Friday), shows no edge. That
asymmetry is the main reason the family is rejected.

## 1. What the strategy does

For each month, let `cpi_day` be the first regular session whose calendar day
of month is >= 12. This is a fixed ex-ante proxy for the CPI release, which is
published at 08:30 ET in the 10th-15th calendar-day window. Then:

```
w_tqqq(k) = 1.00   if k == cpi_day
          = 0.00   otherwise
w_bil(k)  = 1 - w_tqqq(k)
```

- The CPI proxy date is known at the start of the month. The target is set at
  the prior close and filled at the CPI session's open; the exit target (0) is
  set at the CPI session's close and filled at the next open. The harness's
  next-open rule is used unchanged.
- NFP is the first Friday session of the month, a pre-registered control. It is
  not the centre because it has no positive edge in this sample.
- Idle is BIL. The cash-idle variant earns 8.92% at 1 bp, 1.22 pp less; BIL is
  the better idle asset.
- No trend SMA, no realised vol, no drawdown state, no cross-sectional signal,
  no full-sample normalisation.
- The CPI proxy is deliberately **not** the actual historical release date. The
  rule does not hardcode future dates; it can be a few days early or late.

## 2. Headline development result

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | ending equity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | **10.14%** | **26.16%** | **0.65** | 1.03 | 17.1% | $216k |
| 5 bp | 8.04% | 28.08% | 0.54 | 0.85 | 17.0% | $185k |
| 10 bp | 5.46% | 32.27% | 0.40 | 0.62 | 17.0% | $153k |
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1.12 | 66.5% | $1.175m |

| cost | fills | turnover |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 385 | 568.7x |
| 5 bp | 385 | 523.2x |
| 10 bp | 385 | 472.7x |

The strategy is in TQQQ **4.8%** of sessions (96 days out of 2,012) and in BIL
the other 95.2%. The harness `exposure` field is 100% because BIL is an asset;
the mean TQQQ weight is 4.79%. The low exposure is why the CAGR is low: the
conditional mean is strong, but it is earned on only 96 days.

**Drawdown:** the max drawdown is 2022-06-13 to 2022-11-14, **-26.16%**. For a
4.8%-exposed strategy, that is a large DD: the CPI days in 2022 clustered in the
bear market and the strategy was long TQQQ on some of the worst sessions.

**Turnover / fills:** 569x, 385 fills. The strategy enters and exits once a
month; the 2% band is not the main driver.

## 3. Event study: CPI vs NFP

Session-level TQQQ returns, 2016-2023, n = 96 events each. `day` is the event
session open-to-open (the tradable return of holding the event day and selling
at the next open); `oc` is the event session open-to-close; `next` is the
following session open-to-open; `2-day` is day + next.

| event | day mean | day t | day win | day OC | next | 2-day |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **CPI proxy (day 12)** | **+81.9 bp** | **1.94** | 61.5% | +3.9 bp | -13.5 bp | +68.4 bp |
| NFP (first Friday) | +6.7 bp | 0.15 | 59.4% | +46.1 bp | -15.9 bp | -9.2 bp |
| CPI or NFP | +44.3 bp | 1.42 | 60.4% | — | -14.7 bp | +29.6 bp |

The CPI day is the only positive event. The NFP day is flat, and its
open-to-close is actually +46.1 bp (t = 1.38) but it gives it all back
overnight and more (-15.9 bp next), for a negative 2-day. The CPI day's
open-to-close is only +3.9 bp; the day's +81.9 bp is almost all the
close-to-next-open gap (~+78 bp). The next session gives back -13.5 bp, so the
net two-day is +68.4 bp.

This decomposition is the key mechanism finding. If the effect were a
release-day intraday drift, the open-to-close would be positive. It is not. The
effect is a **close-to-next-open** move, which is consistent with the proxy day
being the session before the actual CPI release: the strategy holds through the
release morning and sells at the next open. The rule is ex-ante and captures
that gap, but it is not a "CPI day" intraday effect. The NFP day, which is the
actual release date, has no such gap. That weakens the CPI-specific
interpretation; the proxy may be capturing a mid-month overnight seasonality
rather than a CPI announcement.

CPI-day mean by year (all positive):

| year | n | mean | t | win |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 12 | +111.4 bp | 1.42 | 66.7% |
| 2017 | 12 | +71.3 bp | 2.30 | 75.0% |
| 2018 | 12 | +66.3 bp | 0.85 | 75.0% |
| 2019 | 12 | +71.4 bp | 1.50 | 58.3% |
| 2020 | 12 | +90.2 bp | 0.48 | 58.3% |
| 2021 | 12 | +32.9 bp | 0.40 | 50.0% |
| 2022 | 12 | +31.8 bp | 0.15 | 50.0% |
| 2023 | 12 | +180.1 bp | 1.83 | 58.3% |

The sign is stable, but the magnitude is noisy and 2023 is the largest year.
The 2023 share of the strategy's total log return is about 32%, below the 50%
kill threshold, so the edge is not one year.

## 4. Pre-registered grid

The 8 cells were fixed in `HYPOTHESIS.md` before the final run:

| # | event | window | role | 1 bp CAGR | 1 bp DD | 1 bp Sharpe | 10 bp CAGR |
|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | CPI day 10 | day only | proxy neighbour | 3.40% | 35.52% | 0.30 | -0.99% |
| 2 | CPI day 11 | day only | proxy neighbour | 3.74% | 54.11% | 0.31 | -0.66% |
| 3 | **CPI day 12** | **day only** | **centre** | **10.14%** | **26.16%** | **0.65** | **5.46%** |
| 4 | CPI day 13 | day only | proxy neighbour | 6.03% | 30.29% | 0.43 | 1.53% |
| 5 | CPI day 12 | day + next | window neighbour | 6.78% | 52.12% | 0.40 | 2.24% |
| 6 | CPI day 12 + NFP | day only | combined control | 9.09% | 48.28% | 0.49 | 0.12% |
| 7 | NFP | day only | release control | 0.42% | 43.12% | 0.11 | -3.85% |
| 8 | CPI day 12, 50% | day only | exposure neighbour | 6.03% | 13.43% | 0.72 | 3.73% |

The centre is the **only** cell that clears 5% CAGR at 10 bp (5.46%). The
neighbours at day 10 and day 11 are negative at 10 bp; day 13 is 1.53%. The
proxy is a spike at day 12, not a broad plateau. The NFP-only cell is flat at
1 bp and negative at 10 bp. The CPI+NFP combination is 9.09% at 1 bp but only
0.12% at 10 bp because it doubles the event count and the NFP days add
turnover without mean. The 50% exposure cell has the best Sharpe (0.72) but a
6.03% CAGR; it is a lower-risk version of the same small edge.

## 5. Controls and rejected alternatives

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | comment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **CPI day 12, 100%** | **10.14%** | **26.16%** | **0.65** | centre |
| CPI day 12, 50% | 6.03% | 13.43% | 0.72 | best Sharpe, lower return |
| CPI day 12, cash idle | 8.92% | 26.72% | 0.59 | BIL is better |
| CPI day + next | 6.78% | 52.12% | 0.40 | second session dilutes |
| NFP day + next | -2.53% | 60.12% | 0.00 | negative |
| Pre-release de-risk (100% except pre-event) | 25.59% | 84.74% | 0.68 | high DD, not a standalone |
| TQQQ buy & hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | bar |

The pre-release de-risk is the obvious alternative: hold TQQQ all the time but
go flat on the session before each CPI/NFP release. On the daily approximation
it looked strong, but on the 1-minute panel it earns only 25.59% with an 84.74%
DD, worse than TQQQ on both counts. The 1-minute implementation has 761 fills
and 3,019x turnover; the daily approximation ignored the cost of the pre-release
round trips. It is rejected.

## 6. Placebo

The placebo keeps the same number of event days (96) but chooses them at random.
1,000 draws, daily open-to-open approximation:

| | CAGR |
|---|---:|
| real strategy (1-min, 1 bp) | 10.14% |
| real strategy (daily approximation) | 10.67% |
| placebo mean | 2.66% |
| placebo p95 | 11.12% |
| placebo p99 | 15.11% |
| placebo max | 21.73% |
| p-value (draws >= real) | **0.058** |

The real event days are above the 94th percentile of random 96-day calendars.
The p-value is 0.058, just below the 0.10 kill threshold but not strong. The
real daily approximation (10.67%) is slightly below the placebo p95 (11.12%),
so a random calendar can match the result; the real edge is in the mean, not in
the tail.

## 7. Sub-periods and yearly behaviour

| period | strategy CAGR | strategy DD | TQQQ CAGR | TQQQ DD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 10.49% | 7.99% | 49.67% | 56.77% |
| 2020-2023 | 9.80% | 25.06% | 24.11% | 81.57% |
| **ex-2020** | **10.14%** | **25.06%** | **28.35%** | 81.57% |

| year | strategy | TQQQ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +13.3% | +19.9% |
| 2017 | +9.1% | +114.5% |
| 2018 | +9.1% | -20.8% |
| 2019 | +10.4% | +148.2% |
| 2020 | +8.4% | +104.1% |
| 2021 | +2.9% | +81.1% |
| 2022 | +1.5% | -79.4% |
| 2023 | +28.4% | +192.0% |

The strategy is positive in every year, including 2018 and 2022, because it is
out of the market 95% of the time. It is a low-volatility, low-return sleeve,
not a TQQQ substitute. The 2016-2019 CAGR (10.49%) is slightly higher than
2020-2023 (9.80%), which is a good stability sign; the 2020-2023 DD is much
larger (25.06% vs 7.99%) because the CPI days in 2022 were in the bear market.

## 8. Correlations to the nine current winners

Daily-return Pearson correlation, development window only:

| winner | correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.095 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.147 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.194 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.094 |
| family-session-timing | 0.198 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.234 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.190 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.157 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.190 |

Range **0.094-0.234**, mean **0.167**. This is the lowest correlation of the
four new families and the main reason to keep the study. A 4.8%-exposed
event sleeve with a positive mean and near-zero correlation is a genuine
diversifier, even though it cannot be a standalone return engine.

## 9. Causality and no look-ahead

- The CPI proxy date is the first session on/after calendar day 12, known at the
  start of the month. The NFP proxy is the first Friday session, also known.
  The target is set at the prior close and filled at the next open.
- No actual release dates are hardcoded; the rule can be a few days early or
  late. This is deliberate and is the main source of mechanism uncertainty.
- No warmup indicator is needed; the first decision is 2016-01-04.
- Truncation test: building weights on the panel ending 2022-01-03 leaves all
  weights through 2021-12-29 unchanged (`prior_weights_unchanged: true`).
- No 2024+ bar is loaded in `strategy.py`; the winner-curve correlations are
  truncated to 2023-12-29 before the return calculation.

## 10. Kill criteria and result

| criterion | result | pass? |
|---|---|---|
| 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% | 5.46% | **fail (expected)** |
| CPI day mean not positive or t < 1.5 | +81.9 bp, t = 1.94 | pass |
| CPI not better than NFP | CPI 10.14% vs NFP 0.42%; +81.9 bp vs +6.7 bp | pass |
| random-event placebo p > 0.10 | p = 0.058 | pass |
| 2023 share > 50% of total log | ~35% | pass |
| proxy spike (day 11 and day 13 both negative) | +3.74% / +6.03% at 1 bp; means positive | pass |

The return criterion fails, so the verdict is **negative as a standalone
strategy**. The event-study criteria pass. The family is a valid negative
result with a usable diversifier sleeve.

## 11. Limitations

1. **The CPI proxy is not the release date.** The first session on/after day 12
   can be a few days before or after the actual CPI release. The +81.9 bp is a
   close-to-next-open gap, not an intraday release-day drift. The mechanism may
   be a mid-month overnight seasonality or an accidental alignment with the
   actual release morning, not a CPI-specific announcement effect.
2. **NFP has no edge.** The actual NFP release day is flat (+6.7 bp, t = 0.15).
   If the family were a generic "macro release" effect, NFP should show it. The
   asymmetry is evidence against a simple release-day interpretation.
3. **The proxy is a spike.** Day 10 and day 11 are negative at 10 bp; day 13 is
   1.53%. The centre is the only cell above 5% at 10 bp. A broad plateau would
   be more convincing.
4. **The placebo p = 0.058 is marginal.** The real daily result is below the
   placebo p95. The event mean is positive in all eight years, but the sample
   is only 96 days.
5. **Low exposure means low return.** 4.8% TQQQ weight, 10.14% CAGR at 1 bp,
   5.46% at 10 bp. It cannot replace TQQQ and it is not a standalone strategy.
6. **The 2022 drawdown is 26.16%.** For a 4.8%-exposed sleeve, that is a large
   left tail; the CPI days clustered in the 2022 bear market.

## 12. Final verdict

**The family is rejected as a standalone return strategy but retained as a
positive event study and a low-correlation diversifier.** The deliverable is:

- 10.14% CAGR / 26.16% DD / 0.65 Sharpe at 1 bp;
- 5.46% CAGR / 32.27% DD / 0.40 Sharpe at 10 bp;
- CPI-day mean +81.9 bp (t = 1.94), positive in all eight years;
- NFP day +6.7 bp (t = 0.15), no edge;
- correlation to the nine winners 0.094-0.234;
- random-event placebo p = 0.058;
- exact pre-cut weights (causality truncation test passes).

The honest one-line description: *a 4.8%-exposed TQQQ sleeve that holds the
mid-month CPI proxy session and sells at the next open; the return is a
close-to-next-open gap, not an intraday release-day drift, and the NFP release
day has no edge.* It is useful as a diversifier, not as a replacement for TQQQ.
hypothesis_md:
# Hypothesis: CPI/NFP release windows — the CPI release-day drift

**Slug:** `family-cpi-nfp-release`
**Window:** development only, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, 1-minute marks.
**Bar:** TQQQ dev 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (brief). The
panel's 1 bp TQQQ buy-and-hold is 36.29% / 81.57% / 0.80.
**Status:** pre-registered before the final `strategy.py` run. No 2024+ bar is
loaded anywhere in this directory.

## 1. Claim

Scheduled macro releases are an ex-ante clock. The market prices the release
before the print and then trades the surprise. Two releases dominate the
monthly cycle:

- **NFP** (Employment Situation) is released at 08:30 ET on the first Friday
  of the month (with rare holiday exceptions). The print is before the open,
  so the release-day session contains the full reaction.
- **CPI** is released at 08:30 ET in the 10th-15th calendar-day window. The
  exact date is published in advance but is not fixed; we use a **fixed
  ex-ante proxy**: the first regular session on or after the 12th calendar day
  of the month. The 12th is the midpoint of the official release window. The
  proxy can be a few days early or late; it is deliberately not the actual
  historical release date, so the rule does not hardcode future dates.

The claim is that the **CPI release-day session** has a positive drift: the
pre-release risk premium is paid, the print clears uncertainty, and the index
tends to close higher on the day. The NFP release day is expected to be
weaker: the payroll print is noisier and the reaction is more often a
reversal. The strategy therefore holds TQQQ only on the CPI proxy session,
and uses NFP as a pre-registered control. Both clocks are tested; the family
is not allowed to pick the better one after the fact without disclosure.

This is **not** a trend, volatility, drawdown, opening-range, close-flow,
relative-strength or ML signal. The only inputs are the calendar release
proxies. The decision is known at the prior close.

## 2. Exact rules (centre)

Universe: QQQ (not used), TQQQ (position), BIL (idle).

For each month, let `cpi_day` be the first regular session whose calendar day
of month is >= 12. (If the month has no such session, which cannot happen for
a regular month, the month is skipped.) Then, for session `k`:

```
w_tqqq(k) = 1.00   if k == cpi_day
          = 0.00   otherwise
w_bil(k)  = 1 - w_tqqq(k)
```

- The CPI proxy date is known at the start of the month. The target is set at
  the prior close and filled at the CPI session's open; the exit target (0) is
  set at the CPI session's close and filled at the next open. The harness's
  next-open rule is used unchanged.
- Idle weight is BIL, not cash.
- The 2% rebalance band is the harness default. Headline cost is 1 bp; 5 bp
  and 10 bp are reported.
- No moving average, no realised vol, no drawdown state, no cross-sectional
  signal, no full-sample normalisation.

## 3. Pre-registered grid (8 cells)

The centre is **CPI proxy day, day-only, 100% TQQQ**. The grid is a local
neighbourhood around it, fixed before the final run:

| # | event | window | role |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | CPI, first session on/after day 10 | day only | proxy neighbour |
| 2 | CPI, first session on/after day 11 | day only | proxy neighbour |
| 3 | **CPI, first session on/after day 12** | **day only** | **centre** |
| 4 | CPI, first session on/after day 13 | day only | proxy neighbour |
| 5 | CPI, first session on/after day 12 | day + next | window neighbour |
| 6 | NFP, first Friday | day only | release control |
| 7 | CPI day 12 + NFP day | day only | combined control |
| 8 | CPI day 12, 50% TQQQ | day only | exposure neighbour |

Every cell is reported, including the failures. No cell is selected on the
holdout.

## 4. Pilot scan disclosure

A coarse scan of the dev window was run before fixing the grid. It covered:

- NFP day, NFP-1, NFP+1;
- CPI proxies: first session on/after calendar days 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14;
- the 11th trading session of the month and the second Wednesday;
- release-day, next-session and two-session windows;
- day-only vs a base position with a release overlay.

It showed that the **CPI day-12 proxy** has the strongest release-day mean
(+79.5 bp, t = 1.88, n = 96) and a positive two-session window (+131.5 bp,
t = 2.54). The **NFP day is flat** (+6.1 bp, t = 0.13) and the NFP day+next
window is slightly negative. The combined CPI+NFP window is diluted by NFP.
The CPI day+next window has a lower Sharpe than the day-only version because
the second session adds volatility without adding mean. The centre was fixed
at the day-12 midpoint and day-only before the final run; the other proxies
and NFP are reported as grid cells. The pilot also produced two rejected
ideas reported in `report.md`:

1. **De-risk the pre-release session**: 44.8% gross at 1 bp, but the pre-day
   mean is only -14 bp (t ~ -0.4), it is 2020-tail-driven, and it is not
   "release day/next session only." It is not the delivered centre.
2. **CPI day + next session**: 6.8% at 1 bp, below the day-only centre. The
   second session does not pay for its extra exposure.

## 5. Falsification criteria

The hypothesis is rejected as a standalone strategy if any of the following
holds on the dev window:

1. Centre 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% (the family is expected to fail this; the
   point of the study is the event window, not a TQQQ replacement).
2. The CPI release-day mean is not positive at t >= 1.5.
3. The CPI day is not better than the NFP day on 1 bp CAGR and conditional
   mean.
4. The random-event placebo beats the centre with p > 0.10 (daily
   approximation).
5. The entire CPI effect is one year: 2023 contributes more than 50% of the
   total log return.
6. The CPI day-12 proxy is a spike: the day-11 and day-13 neighbours both
   have negative conditional means.

Criterion 2 is the event-study test. Criterion 1 is the return test. The
family can pass the event study and fail the return test; that is a valid
negative result, and it must be reported that way.

## 6. What would make this a real holdout candidate

The strategy is in TQQQ only about 4.8% of sessions, so it cannot replace
TQQQ. Its value is as a **diversifier**: a low-correlation, positive-mean
event sleeve that can be layered on a core book. It is a candidate for the
one-shot holdout only as an event sleeve, not as a standalone return engine.
If the CPI-day mean is not stable across sub-periods or the random-event
placebo is as good, the honest verdict is "no event edge."

## Own test

"""CPI/NFP release windows: the CPI release-day drift.

Standalone strategy, development window only (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).

Rules
-----
For each month, let `cpi_day` be the first regular session whose calendar day
of month is >= 12.  This is a fixed ex-ante proxy for the CPI release, which
is published at 08:30 ET in the 10th-15th calendar-day window.  Then:

    w_tqqq(k) = 1.00   if k == cpi_day
              = 0.00   otherwise
    w_bil(k)  = 1 - w_tqqq(k)

The CPI proxy date is known at the start of the month.  The target is set at
the prior close and filled at the CPI session's open; the exit target (0) is
set at the CPI session's close and filled at the next open.

NFP (first Friday of the month) is a pre-registered control, not the centre:
the NFP day is flat on average in this sample, while the CPI day is positive.
The delivered centre is (cpi_day_offset=12, window=1, weight=1.00).  The
8-cell pre-registered grid is in HYPOTHESIS.md.  No 2024+ bar is loaded.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START = "2016-01-04"
DEV_END = "2023-12-29"
BARS_1M = 252 * 390
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")
COL_Q, COL_T, COL_B = 0, 1, 2

# pre-registered centre
CPI_DAY = 12
CPI_WINDOW = 1
CPI_WEIGHT = 1.00

BAR = {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229, "sharpe": 0.82}
PANEL_BAR = {"cagr": 0.3629, "max_drawdown": 0.8157, "sharpe": 0.80}

WINNERS = (
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# calendar and weights
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def calendar(ts):
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)
    sd = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(dates[first]))
    dom = sd.dt.day.to_numpy()
    dow = sd.dt.day_of_week.to_numpy()
    month = sd.dt.month.to_numpy()
    year = sd.dt.year.to_numpy()
    month_id = year * 100 + month
    return {"dates": dates, "first": first, "last": last, "nd": nd,
            "dom": dom, "dow": dow, "month": month, "year": year,
            "month_id": month_id}


def event_days(cal, cpi_day=CPI_DAY, include_nfp=False):
    """Boolean per-session flags for the CPI proxy and the NFP proxy."""
    nd = cal["nd"]
    cpi = np.zeros(nd, dtype=bool)
    nfp = np.zeros(nd, dtype=bool)
    for m in np.unique(cal["month_id"]):
        idx = np.flatnonzero(cal["month_id"] == m)
        hit = idx[cal["dom"][idx] >= cpi_day]
        if len(hit):
            cpi[hit[0]] = True
        fri = idx[cal["dow"][idx] == 4]
        if len(fri):
            nfp[fri[0]] = True
    return cpi, nfp


def window_flag(flag, length):
    """True for `length` consecutive sessions starting at each event day."""
    out = flag.copy()
    for j in range(1, length):
        out = out | np.r_[flag[j:], np.zeros(j, dtype=bool)]
    return out


def weights_from_target(ts, first, last, nd, target, idle_bil=True):
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    for k in range(nd):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        x = float(target[k])
        w[f:l, COL_T] = x
        if idle_bil:
            w[f:l, COL_B] = 1.0 - x
        xn = float(target[k + 1]) if k + 1 < nd else x
        w[l, COL_T] = xn
        if idle_bil:
            w[l, COL_B] = 1.0 - xn
    assert w.min() >= -1e-12, "negative weight"
    assert np.all(w.sum(axis=1) <= 1.0 + 1e-9), "weights sum > 1"
    return w


def build_weights_params(ts, o, c, cpi_day=CPI_DAY, window=CPI_WINDOW,
                         weight=CPI_WEIGHT, include_nfp=False,
                         idle_bil=True):
    cal = calendar(ts)
    cpi, nfp = event_days(cal, cpi_day=cpi_day)
    flag = cpi | nfp if include_nfp else cpi
    flag = window_flag(flag, window)
    target = flag.astype(float) * weight
    return weights_from_target(ts, cal["first"], cal["last"], cal["nd"],
                               target, idle_bil=idle_bil)


def build_weights(ts, o, c):
    """Pre-registered centre."""
    return build_weights_params(ts, o, c)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# evaluation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def pack(s):
    keys = ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
            "exposure", "turnover", "fills", "ending_equity", "years")
    return {k: (int(s[k]) if k == "fills" else float(s[k])) for k in keys}


def run_weights(ts, o, c, w, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START):
    res = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    return res, bt.stats(res, BARS_1M)


def daily_equity(res):
    s = pd.Series(res["equity"], index=res["ts"])
    d = s.groupby(res["ts"].date).last()
    d.index = pd.to_datetime(d.index)
    return d


def annual_returns(de, start_equity=100_000.0):
    out = {}
    prev = start_equity
    for year in range(2016, 2024):
        x = de[de.index.year == year]
        if len(x) == 0:
            continue
        out[str(year)] = float(x.iloc[-1] / prev - 1.0)
        prev = x.iloc[-1]
    return out


def subperiod(de, lo, hi):
    x = de[(de.index >= lo) & (de.index <= hi)]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return None
    years = (x.index[-1] - x.index[0]).days / 365.25
    return {"cagr": float((x.iloc[-1] / x.iloc[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
            "max_drawdown": float(-(x / x.cummax() - 1).min()),
            "years": float(years)}


def dd_window(ts, equity):
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
    dd = equity / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    i = int(np.argmax(equity[: j + 1]))
    return {"peak": str(ts[i])[:10], "trough": str(ts[j])[:10],
            "dd": float(-dd[j])}


def daily_frame(ts, o, c):
    cal = calendar(ts)
    first, last, nd = cal["first"], cal["last"], cal["nd"]
    t_open = np.asarray(o)[first, COL_T]
    t_close = np.asarray(c)[last, COL_T]
    b_open = np.asarray(o)[first, COL_B]
    q_open = np.asarray(o)[first, COL_Q]
    q_close = np.asarray(c)[last, COL_Q]
    t_oo = np.r_[t_open[1:] / t_open[:-1] - 1.0, 0.0]
    b_oo = np.r_[b_open[1:] / b_open[:-1] - 1.0, 0.0]
    q_oo = np.r_[q_open[1:] / q_open[:-1] - 1.0, 0.0]
    t_oc = t_close / t_open - 1.0
    q_oc = q_close / q_open - 1.0
    return {"cal": cal, "t_oo": t_oo, "b_oo": b_oo, "q_oo": q_oo,
            "t_oc": t_oc, "q_oc": q_oc}


def daily_cagr(frac, frame, idle_bil=True):
    r = frac * frame["t_oo"]
    if idle_bil:
        r = r + (1.0 - frac) * frame["b_oo"]
    eq = np.cumprod(1.0 + r)
    years = len(r) / 252.0
    return float(eq[-1] ** (1 / years) - 1.0)


def stat(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
    n = len(x)
    if n < 2:
        return {"n": int(n), "mean_bp": float("nan"), "t": float("nan"),
                "win": float("nan"), "sd_bp": float("nan")}
    return {"n": int(n), "mean_bp": float(np.mean(x) * 1e4),
            "t": float(np.mean(x) / (np.std(x, ddof=0) / np.sqrt(n))),
            "win": float((x > 0).mean()),
            "sd_bp": float(np.std(x, ddof=0) * 1e4)}


def correlation_to_winners(r):
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
        d = json.loads(path.read_text())
        idx = pd.to_datetime(d["dates"])
        v = pd.Series(d["values"], index=idx)
        v = v[v.index <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)]
        rr = v.pct_change().dropna()
        j = pd.concat([r, rr], axis=1, join="inner").dropna()
        out[slug] = float(j.iloc[:, 0].corr(j.iloc[:, 1]))
    vals = np.array(list(out.values()))
    return {"by_slug": out, "min": float(vals.min()),
            "max": float(vals.max()), "mean": float(vals.mean())}


def causality_check(ts, o, c, builder):
    j = bt.start_index(ts, "2022-01-03")
    j2 = bt.start_index(ts, "2021-12-30")
    w_trunc = builder(ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j])
    w_full = builder(ts, o, c)
    return {"truncation_date": "2022-01-03", "compare_through": "2021-12-29",
            "prior_weights_unchanged": bool(np.allclose(w_trunc[:j2], w_full[:j2]))}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main():
    ts, o, c = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min", warmup_days=5)
    cal = calendar(ts)
    frame = daily_frame(ts, o, c)
    nd = cal["nd"]
    print(f"panel {len(ts):,} bars, {nd} sessions, "
          f"{ts[0].date()} .. {ts[-1].date()}")

    w = build_weights(ts, o, c)
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, DEV_START)
    bench_bars = np.asarray(c)[i0:, COL_T]
    bench = bt.benchmark(bench_bars, ts[i0:], BARS_1M)

    out = {
        "strategy": "family-cpi-nfp-release",
        "directory": "research/new/family-cpi-nfp-release",
        "window": {"start": DEV_START, "end": DEV_END, "marks": "1m",
                   "fills": "next open, 2% band", "idle": "BIL"},
        "rules": {
            "clock": "CPI proxy = first session on/after calendar day 12; "
                     "NFP proxy = first Friday session",
            "cpi_day_offset": CPI_DAY,
            "cpi_window": CPI_WINDOW,
            "cpi_weight": CPI_WEIGHT,
            "nfp_role": "control, not centre",
            "cpi_assumption": "CPI is released at 08:30 ET in the 10th-15th "
                              "calendar-day window; day 12 is the midpoint "
                              "proxy, not the actual release date",
            "bar": BAR,
            "panel_bar": PANEL_BAR,
        },
        "dev": {},
    }

    results = {}
    for slip in (1.0, 5.0, 10.0):
        res, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, w, slip=slip)
        results[slip] = (res, s)
        out["dev"][f"{int(slip)}bp"] = pack(s)
        print(f"centre {slip:2.0f}bp  CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
              f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sharpe {s['sharpe']:4.2f}  "
              f"fills {s['fills']:,}  turnover {s['turnover']:.0f}  "
              f"exposure {s['exposure']*100:.1f}%")

    res1, s1 = results[1.0]
    out["benchmark_tqqq"] = {k: float(v) for k, v in bench.items()}
    out["benchmark_tqqq"]["symbol"] = "TQQQ"
    out["benchmark_tqqq"]["bar_from_brief"] = BAR
    print(f"bench  CAGR {bench['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {bench['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {bench['sharpe']:4.2f}")

    wbar = w[:, COL_T]
    wsess = w[cal["first"], COL_T]
    out["exposure"] = {
        "mean_tqqq_weight_bar": float(wbar.mean()),
        "mean_tqqq_weight_session": float(wsess.mean()),
        "fraction_sessions_in": float((wsess > 0.99).mean()),
        "fraction_sessions_out": float((wsess < 0.01).mean()),
        "mean_bil_weight": float(w[:, COL_B].mean()),
        "stats_exposure_incl_bil": float(s1["exposure"]),
    }
    print("exposure", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in out["exposure"].items()})

    de = daily_equity(res1)
    r = de.pct_change().dropna()
    out["yearly"] = {
        y: {"strategy": v,
            "benchmark": float(bt.yearly(res1["ts"], res1["equity"],
                                         bench_bars)[int(y)]["benchmark"])}
        for y, v in annual_returns(de).items()
    }
    out["dd_window"] = dd_window(res1["ts"], res1["equity"])
    out["subperiods"] = {
        "2016_2019": subperiod(de, "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
        "2020_2023": subperiod(de, "2020-01-02", "2023-12-29"),
    }
    ex = de[de.index.year != 2020]
    yrs = (ex.index[-1] - ex.index[0]).days / 365.25
    out["ex2020"] = {"cagr": float((ex.iloc[-1] / ex.iloc[0]) ** (1 / yrs) - 1),
                     "max_drawdown": float(-(ex / ex.cummax() - 1).min())}

    # ---- event diagnostics --------------------------------------------------
    cpi, nfp = event_days(cal)
    ev = cpi | nfp
    prev = np.r_[False, ev[:-1]]
    nxt = np.r_[ev[1:], False]
    rows = []
    for name, flag in (("cpi_day12", cpi), ("nfp_first_friday", nfp),
                       ("cpi_or_nfp", ev)):
        rows.append({
            "event": name,
            "n": int(flag.sum()),
            "day_tqqq_oo": stat(frame["t_oo"][flag]),
            "day_tqqq_oc": stat(frame["t_oc"][flag]),
            "day_qqq_oo": stat(frame["q_oo"][flag]),
            "day_qqq_oc": stat(frame["q_oc"][flag]),
            "pre_tqqq_oo": stat(frame["t_oo"][np.r_[False, flag[:-1]]]),
            "next_tqqq_oo": stat(frame["t_oo"][np.r_[flag[1:], False]]),
            "two_day_tqqq_oo": stat(frame["t_oo"][flag] +
                                    frame["t_oo"][np.r_[flag[1:], False]]),
        })
    out["event_diagnostics"] = rows
    for row in rows:
        print(f"{row['event']:18s} n={row['n']:3d} day {row['day_tqqq_oo']['mean_bp']:+7.1f}bp "
              f"t {row['day_tqqq_oo']['t']:+5.2f}  next {row['next_tqqq_oo']['mean_bp']:+7.1f}bp  "
              f"2day {row['two_day_tqqq_oo']['mean_bp']:+7.1f}bp")

    # by-year CPI-day mean
    by_year = []
    for y in range(2016, 2024):
        m = cpi & (cal["year"] == y)
        by_year.append({"year": y, "n": int(m.sum()),
                        **stat(frame["t_oo"][m])})
    out["cpi_day_by_year"] = by_year
    print("CPI day by year", [(d["year"], round(d["mean_bp"], 1)) for d in by_year])

    # ---- pre-registered grid (8 cells) --------------------------------------
    grid_spec = [
        (10, 1, 1.0, False, "proxy neighbour"),
        (11, 1, 1.0, False, "proxy neighbour"),
        (12, 1, 1.0, False, "centre"),
        (13, 1, 1.0, False, "proxy neighbour"),
        (12, 2, 1.0, False, "window neighbour"),
        (12, 1, 1.0, True, "CPI+NFP control"),
        (12, 1, 1.0, False, "NFP-only control"),
        (12, 1, 0.5, False, "exposure neighbour"),
    ]
    grid = []
    for cpi_day, window, weight, inc_nfp, role in grid_spec:
        if role == "NFP-only control":
            # special case: NFP only is not expressible with the CPI builder
            cpi_f, nfp_f = event_days(cal)
            flag = window_flag(nfp_f, window)
            target = flag.astype(float) * weight
            wt = weights_from_target(ts, cal["first"], cal["last"], nd,
                                     target, idle_bil=True)
            event = "nfp_only"
        else:
            wt = build_weights_params(ts, o, c, cpi_day=cpi_day, window=window,
                                      weight=weight, include_nfp=inc_nfp)
            event = "cpi_plus_nfp" if inc_nfp else "cpi_only"
        _, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
        _, s10 = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt, slip=10.0)
        grid.append({"cpi_day": cpi_day, "window": window, "weight": weight,
                     "include_nfp": inc_nfp, "event": event, "role": role,
                     **pack(s), "ten_bp": pack(s10)})
        print(f"grid cpi={cpi_day} win={window} w={weight:.2f} nfp={inc_nfp} "
              f"{role:20s} 1bp CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
              f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {s['sharpe']:.2f}  "
              f"10bp CAGR {s10['cagr']*100:6.2f}%")
    out["grid"] = grid

    # ---- controls -----------------------------------------------------------
    controls = {}
    wt = build_weights_params(ts, o, c, cpi_day=12, window=1, weight=1.0,
                              include_nfp=False, idle_bil=False)
    _, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
    controls["centre_cash_idle"] = pack(s)
    print(f"control centre cash idle   CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
          f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {s['sharpe']:.2f}")

    # pre-release de-risk: the rejected alternative, disclosed
    cpi_f, nfp_f = event_days(cal)
    ev_f = cpi_f | nfp_f
    pre = np.r_[False, ev_f[:-1]]
    target = (~pre).astype(float)
    wt = weights_from_target(ts, cal["first"], cal["last"], nd, target,
                             idle_bil=True)
    _, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
    controls["pre_release_derisk_100_except_pre"] = pack(s)
    print(f"control pre-release de-risk CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
          f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {s['sharpe']:.2f}")

    # NFP day + next
    flag = window_flag(nfp_f, 2)
    target = flag.astype(float)
    wt = weights_from_target(ts, cal["first"], cal["last"], nd, target,
                             idle_bil=True)
    _, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
    controls["nfp_day_plus_next"] = pack(s)
    print(f"control NFP day+next       CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
          f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {s['sharpe']:.2f}")

    # CPI day + next
    flag = window_flag(cpi_f, 2)
    target = flag.astype(float)
    wt = weights_from_target(ts, cal["first"], cal["last"], nd, target,
                             idle_bil=True)
    _, s = run_weights(ts, o, c, wt)
    controls["cpi_day_plus_next"] = pack(s)
    print(f"control CPI day+next       CAGR {s['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
          f"DD {s['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sh {s['sharpe']:.2f}")
    out["controls"] = controls

    # ---- placebo ------------------------------------------------------------
    n_event = int(cpi.sum())
    real_daily = daily_cagr(cpi.astype(float), frame, idle_bil=True)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261127)
    draws = []
    base = np.zeros(nd)
    for _ in range(1000):
        mask = rng.choice(nd, n_event, replace=False)
        f = base.copy()
        f[mask] = 1.0
        draws.append(daily_cagr(f, frame, idle_bil=True))
    draws = np.array(draws)
    out["placebo"] = {
        "n_draws": int(len(draws)), "marks": "1D open-to-open",
        "n_event_days": n_event,
        "real_daily_cagr": float(real_daily),
        "real_1m_cagr_1bp": float(s1["cagr"]),
        "mean": float(draws.mean()),
        "p95": float(np.quantile(draws, 0.95)),
        "p99": float(np.quantile(draws, 0.99)),
        "max": float(draws.max()),
        "p_value": float((draws >= real_daily).mean()),
    }
    print("placebo", {k: (round(v, 4) if isinstance(v, float) else v)
                      for k, v in out["placebo"].items()})

    # ---- correlations -------------------------------------------------------
    out["correlation"] = correlation_to_winners(r)
    print("corr winners min %.3f max %.3f mean %.3f" % (
        out["correlation"]["min"], out["correlation"]["max"],
        out["correlation"]["mean"]))
    print("corr", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in out["correlation"]["by_slug"].items()})

    # ---- causality ----------------------------------------------------------
    out["causality"] = causality_check(ts, o, c, build_weights)
    print("causality", out["causality"])

    # ---- kill criteria ------------------------------------------------------
    dev10 = out["dev"]["10bp"]
    cpi_row = [x for x in rows if x["event"] == "cpi_day12"][0]
    nfp_row = [x for x in rows if x["event"] == "nfp_first_friday"][0]
    c1 = dev10["cagr"] <= BAR["cagr"]
    c2 = cpi_row["day_tqqq_oo"]["mean_bp"] <= 0 or cpi_row["day_tqqq_oo"]["t"] < 1.5
    c3 = not (cpi_row["day_tqqq_oo"]["mean_bp"] > nfp_row["day_tqqq_oo"]["mean_bp"]
              and s1["cagr"] > [g for g in grid if g["role"] == "NFP-only control"][0]["cagr"])
    c4 = out["placebo"]["p_value"] > 0.10
    yr = out["yearly"]
    log_total = sum(np.log1p(v["strategy"]) for v in yr.values())
    log_2023 = np.log1p(yr["2023"]["strategy"])
    c5 = log_2023 / log_total > 0.50 if log_total > 0 else False
    # neighbour conditional means, computed directly
    c11 = event_days(cal, cpi_day=11)[0]
    c13 = event_days(cal, cpi_day=13)[0]
    c6 = (stat(frame["t_oo"][c11])["mean_bp"] <= 0
          and stat(frame["t_oo"][c13])["mean_bp"] <= 0)
    kills = {
        "c1_10bp_cagr_below_bar": bool(c1),
        "c2_cpi_day_mean_or_t_fails": bool(c2),
        "c3_cpi_not_better_than_nfp": bool(c3),
        "c4_placebo_p_above_0.10": bool(c4),
        "c5_2023_share_above_half": bool(c5),
        "c6_proxy_spike": bool(c6),
    }
    out["kill_criteria"] = kills
    out["verdict"] = "negative" if any(kills.values()) else "positive"
    print("kill criteria", kills)
    print("verdict", out["verdict"])

    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
